title: Mixed-batch + persistent-KV long-context quant bench & calibration audit
creator: Asha Patel
description: Objective: validate FP8 and INT8 quantization profiles across realistic production serving patterns that combine mixed batch sizes, long-context workloads with persistent KV/prefix caching, and streaming tail-latency constraints. We need to prove that calibrated variants meet accuracy SLAs and measure throughput/latency trade-offs vs FP16 baseline.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration workflow produces stable scales across 3 independent runs (max variance < 0.5% per-tensor)
INT8 tuned profile: <0.8% LM perplexity regression vs FP16 baseline on evaluation set (held-out 5k prompts)
FP8 profile: <1.5% regression and no tail-latency > 2x baseline for 95th pctiles under production mix
Throughput: quantized variant achieves >=1.6x tokens/sec vs FP16 when batching is enabled (batch sizes 1/4/8 distribution 50/30/20)
End-to-end 95th percentile latency with KV-cache warm: not worse than 1.8x FP16 baseline for common short requests (seq_len 512)
plan: Define calibration datasets and sampling: 3 datasets (in-domain prompts, long-context synthetic continuations, edge-case system prompts), 5k examples total

Implement deterministic calibration runner that supports per-layer and per-channel schemes (reuse existing calib harness but add RNG seed and run metadata), commit under GH: redwood-inference/quant-calib#PR-482
Create benchmark harness that simulates production request mix: batch size distribution, seq_len distribution (64/512/4096), KV warm/cold paths, and streaming toggles

Run controlled sweep across FP8/INT8 quant profiles, per-layer vs per-channel, and activation clip strategies; collect latency (p50/p95/p99), tokens/sec, and quality metrics (perplexity, response-level similarity)
Surface results in a dashboard: Grafana board runtime/quantization/bench-ENG-22350 (temporary) and attach artifacts to Confluence: /confluence/display/INF/ENG-22350-QuantAudit
Review with ML researchers and runtime owners; decide which profile(s) to include as 'verified' in model catalog
experiment_matrix: Quant variants: FP16 baseline, INT8 per-layer, INT8 per-channel, FP8 dynamic, FP8 static-calib
Batching modes: no batching (batch=1), opportunistic batching (autoscaler), persistent batching (internal pool), mixed-batch trace (50% b1,30% b4,20% b8)
KV-cache states: cold (first token), warm (after prefix cached), sticky (cache reused across requests for same session)
Sequence lengths: short(64), medium(512), long(4096), multi-chunk streaming (continuous 8192 tokens)
Calibration strategies: global-minmax, per-tensor-mean-std, KL-divergence clipping, percentile(99.9)
progress_updates: 2026-02-16: Kickoff meeting with Research (Jin Park) and Runtime (Marco). Agreed dataset slices and initial success thresholds.
2026-02-18: Implemented deterministic seed for calibration runner and added run metadata. Branch: feat/quant-calib-determinism. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quant-calib/pull/482
2026-02-22: First sweep on redwood-7B-causal completed (INT8 per-layer). Observed tokens/sec +1.55x vs FP16 for mixed-batch but p95 latency increased 1.9x for cold-KV longseq — flagged for follow-up.
2026-02-25: FP8 static-calib run produced unstable activation scales between runs (variance ~1.8%). Added more representative long-context samples to calibration set and re-ran.

2026-03-01: Re-run after adding long-context samples; FP8 variance dropped to 0.4% across runs for redwood-7B. Early accuracy matches within 1.2% perplexity. Preparing full sweep across models next week.
results_summary: Preliminary: INT8 per-channel gives best stability/accuracy balance for medium and short seqs; throughput improvement 1.5-1.8x typical. FP8 yields larger throughput gains (~2.0x) but required expanded calibration set to stabilize long-context behavior. Tail latency regressions observed primarily on cold-KV long-context streaming paths when opportunistic batching collides with cache warm-up; mitigations proposed below.
observations_and_tradeoffs: Opportunistic batching increases overall throughput but can amplify cold-KV long-context tail latency; recommended to gate aggressive batching for requests with long prefix tokens or enable KV-aware batching policies
Per-channel INT8 calibration is more compute-expensive during build but yields lower perplexity delta than per-layer for certain attention-heavy layers
FP8 requires careful outlier handling (percentile clipping) which can be sensitive to dataset skew; over-clipping reduces expressivity and increases perplexity
Runtime mitigations (serve-side): adaptive batch sizing based on detected prefix length; prioritized cache warm paths for sessions with long-context workloads
open_questions: Do we accept a slightly higher p95 latency for long-context FP8 variants if throughput wins are >1.9x for interactive workloads?
Should the model catalog include both INT8 and FP8 profiles with runtime routing policies, or only promote INT8 as default for Dedicated customers?
What is the operational cost of adding deterministic multi-run calibration to CI for every model version?
next_steps: Finish full model sweep by 2026-03-05 and push consolidated results to Confluence
Prototype KV-aware batching policy in runtime canary and measure tail-latency impact (ENG-22361 as follow-up)
Write a short PRD recommending catalog promotion rules (criteria: accuracy delta, p95 latency bound, throughput multiplier)
Schedule review with Product (Maya Singh) and Research (Jin Park) on 2026-03-08
